features.description: Wrong-worktree refusal (moved from worktree-isolation-v0 F003 at its D012 split): every plan-mutating entry point shares one fail-closed guard precondition built on v0's canonical binding_health predicate.
features.acceptance: `plan lock`, `plan audit`, `plan close`, `plan disposition`, and the orchestrate dispatch entry point share ONE guard precondition evaluated BEFORE any gate side effect or evidence write: the registry loads via the STRICT path (a corrupt registry file FAILS CLOSED with a distinct registry-corrupt error naming the file — never the unbound passthrough); when the plan has a binding, the invoking working tree (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) must equal the bound worktree_path with BOTH sides fully resolved (symlinks and relative components canonicalized via realpath-equivalent resolution) before comparison — symlinked or case-variant spellings of the same directory neither falsely refuse nor falsely pass AND the binding must pass the canonical binding_health predicate (F004 — the guard CALLS it, never re-specifies health conditions), so a deleted worktree replaced by an unrelated repository at the same path and branch refuses with the predicate's reason; any unhealthy or indeterminate state refuses fail-closed naming the failed conjunct plus the exact create/override commands; an explicit override flag with a required reason proceeds and records the override (plan_id, invoking path, bound path, reason, actor, timestamp) into the plan's audit evidence AND still captures the F002 binding snapshot (a combined override-path test asserts both artifacts land); plans with no binding in a VALID (or absent) registry are never refused (backward-compatibility regression test); DontPanic has NO merge command — merging is the operator's external gh ritual, so the guarded set above IS the complete plan-mutating surface, and this feature OWNS that guard with a CLI-surface test asserting the plan command namespace exposes no merge subcommand; tests cover refusal per guarded entry point, each binding_health conjunct refusal through the guard, corrupt-registry refusal, override-with-reason recording plus snapshot capture, and the unbound passthrough.

features.description: Explicit, audited, safe cleanup (moved from worktree-isolation-v0 F005 at its D012 split): health-gated, audit-first, no-force removal.
features.acceptance: `dontpanic plan worktree remove <plan-id>` loads the registry via the STRICT path (refusing on a corrupt registry file before touching any filesystem state) and is eligible to remove ONLY a binding that passes the canonical binding_health predicate (F004 — called, not re-specified) AND whose worktree is fully clean — PINNED: no modified, staged, or untracked files per porcelain default mode; gitignored files do NOT block removal and are deleted with the worktree (they are regenerable by declaration); any nested .git directory under the worktree that is not a registered submodule of the repo BLOCKS removal with its path reported (it may hold work invisible to porcelain); an unhealthy binding refuses naming the predicate's failed conjunct; a dirty tree refuses printing the offending paths; eligible removal is ORDERED audit-first: the audit entry is appended and flushed BEFORE any destructive step, and if the audit append fails the removal does not proceed (an unaudited cleanup is impossible by construction); only then does it run git worktree remove WITHOUT --force and delete the registry binding; the audit entry records (plan_id, worktree_path, branch, owner_actor, removed_by — the actor performing the cleanup, resolved the same way as owner_actor and recorded even when it differs — and removed_at) to a worktree audit log under $DONTPANIC_HOME; no command in this plan deletes a dirty worktree or exposes a force-removal flag (asserted by a CLI-surface test); `plan close` performs NO worktree removal — at most it prints the explicit remove command (regression test on the close path); tests cover clean removal with audit entry, the unwritable-audit-log refusal (worktree untouched), dirty refusal listing files, untracked-only refusal, refusal for each unhealthy-binding conjunct, corrupt-registry refusal, and the close-does-not-remove guarantee.
